name: Gweike G2 Max 50W Fiber
tagline: 50W Desktop fiber marker for metal and select plastics
tldr: Gweike G2 Max 50W Fiber is the 50W SKU on the Gweike gweike g2 line. Gweike G2 packages a 20W fiber galvo in a desktop form factor. Verify optical power on the listing: do not assume combined-watt marketing.
mainObjective: Production-leaning fiber marking for small businesses

priceRange.note: Official Gweike store, Oct 2026: $2,499 depending on electric lift

engraveExample.description: Filled logo on stainless steel plate

pros: Deepest engraving in the G2 line: about 4.5 mm in brass in Gweike's two-hour test, rated up to 5 mm on metal
Cuts 0.5 mm brass in about 4 passes at 10 mm/s (Gweike demo), the fastest G2 for jewelry blanks
Ships with the 150 mm lens and electric lift as standard
cons: At $2,499 it costs about as much as some split-cabinet fiber machines with a larger chassis
Same compact chassis and 150 mm field as the cheaper G2 models: more power, not more work area
Still Q-switched: no MOPA colour control despite the higher price

faq.question: How deep does the G2 Max 50W engrave?
faq.answer: Gweike rates it for up to 5 mm on metal with enough passes. In its comparison video, two hours at 1,000 mm/s reached about 4.5 mm in brass, and one hour reached 3.2 mm in slate. Depth per pass is far lower: relief work means many repeated passes.

faq.question: Can the 50W cut thin brass or silver for jewelry?
faq.answer: Thin stock, yes. Gweike's demo cuts 0.5 mm brass at 10 mm/s in 4 passes. Expect more passes on thicker or more reflective metals such as silver, and an edge that may need light finishing. It does not replace a sheet-metal cutter.

faq.question: Is the G2 Max worth $700 more than the G2 Pro?
faq.answer: At $2,499 (Gweike US store, October 2026) against $1,799 for the Pro in the same 150 mm electric configuration, the extra money buys depth and fewer passes, not finer detail or colour. It pays off if you cut blanks or engrave deep every week; for surface marking the Pro does the same job.

standoutFeatures.title: Deep engraving in a portable unit
standoutFeatures.body: Gweike rates the G2 Max for up to 5 mm on metal. Its own test reached 4.5 mm in brass after two hours, more than twice the 2.1 mm of the entry G2, in a machine of about 6.5 kg.

standoutFeatures.title: The practical G2 for thin cut-outs
standoutFeatures.body: Four passes through 0.5 mm brass at 10 mm/s in Gweike's demo, against seven on the Pro and eleven on the entry G2. For pendants, tags and small brass parts, that is the gap between a usable and a tedious workflow.

beginnerNotes: This profile is the 50W SKU on Gweike G2 Max Fiber. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Batch similar jobs to reduce setup. Use rotary only when quotes include cylinder work: it slows flat-stock days.
primaryUse: Mid-power fiber for shops marking metal daily

editorialDepth.advantages: Gweike G2 Max Fiber 50W fits shops that mark stainless, aluminum, and tools daily without a CO₂ bay. A solid bench option for jewelry, tags, and small batches.
editorialDepth.limitations: Skip if wood, leather, or cast acrylic pay your bills. Deep metal cutting and large industrial panels often need more fiber headroom or a different machine class.
